definition: a. 突然的, 唐突的, 陡峭的, 不连贯的
EN: Terminating suddenly; appearing to be cut off transversely; truncate. For example, the stipe of some Hohenbuehelia has this characteristic.
EN: Separation, such as a spore detaching from a sporogenous cell. From Latin abscissio, breaking off.

EN: A method of spore formation in fungi characterized by abjunction and then abscission. Spores are produced in a sporogenous filament. In abjunction, they are then separated by transverse walls or septa, with the result spores are grouped in short chains. In abscission, successive portions are cut off and released.
EN: Organisms that can grow in high-acidity environments; in mycology, lichens that can grow in peaty soil or on acidic tree bark.
EN: A chain of conidia where new spores are formed at the apex, with the oldest at the base. Compare with basipetal.
EN: Formed at the apex and along the sides; e.g. conidia of Trichothecium.

EN: Conidium of Emmonsia parva. A large spore that increases notably in size, but does not divide. Upon being inhalted in the lungs of humans and animals, can cause adiaspiromycosis disease. From Gr. a-, without, dia, separating.
EN: Adhering; attached to the stipe throughout its width, esp. of lamellae or tubes. Compare with free.
EN: Aquatic fungi that grow in water, but spread their spores via air.
(pl. aethalia) 粘菌(孢子体), 块状复孢囊
EN: The relatively large fruiting body of many slime molds (Myxomycetes). From Gr. aíthalos, soot.

EN: A member of the order Agaricales; a mushroom or toadstool. Contains many iconic and highly studied fungi. Agarics have a macroscopic (human-visible) fleshy basidioma with a clearly differentiated stipe (stalk), pileus (cap), and lamellae (gills) on the underside of the pileus.
EN: A single-celled, non-septate cell in mitosporic fungi; compare with dictyospore and phragmospore.
EN: An asexual state of a fungus, characterized by the presence of conidia and the absence of sexual spores.
EN: Fusion between branches of hyphae to make a network.

EN: A type of blastic conidiogenesis. The conidiogenous cell (also called an annellide) produces a basipetal sequence of conidia called annelloconidia or annellospores. The distal end is marked by ring-shaped bands called annellations. Examples include many aquatic Hyphomycetes, Venturia inaequalis, and Microascus brevicaulis.
EN: 1. Ring-like; an arrangement in the style of a ring.
n. 环, 环形物, 体环
EN: A ring-like covering around the stipe after expansion of the pileus.
EN: The male sexual organ (gametangium) of fungi. Produces either antherozoids (flagellate gametes or sperm) or gametic nuclei.
EN: At the tip or end (apex).
EN: A short projection at the end of a spore.
EN: A non-motile asexual spore in some Zygomycetes, contained in globose sporangia or cylindrical merosporangia. From Gr. planos, roaming.
EN: Having no stem or pedicel, such as a pileus lacking a stipe and directly attached to the substrate. Found in sporangia of Perichanea for example. From Gr. podos, foot.
EN: A swelling or a swollen filament. Associated with the swollen end of a sporangiophore in Mucorales or the protuberance found beneath the sporocarp of some fungi, especially Protosteliales.
n. [植]子囊盘的(某些子囊菌和地衣的产孢子结构)
EN: A type of fruiting body that, at maturity, opens to expose the hymenium of asci; commonly assumes shape of a cup or saucer. The stipe is sometimes lichenized. From Gr. apotheke, storehouse.
a. 紧贴的, 紧靠的
EN: Flattened, or closely applied; e.g. of scales or fibers.

EN: A swelling at the end of a germ tube or other hypha that adheres to the surface of its host and penetrates it with infection hyphae. Characteristic of plant pathogenic fungi such as Phytophthora and Colletotrichum, as well as parasites of animals such as Entomophthora.

EN: Fungi that live in water. Sometimes subdivided into freshwater-living fungi and marine fungi for saltwater-living fungi. Freshwater fungi include: Many zoosporic fungi of Chytridiomycota, Chytridiales, and Saprolegniales; some saxicolous lichens of Lichinaceae that live on submerged rocks; aquatic hyphomycetes or Ingoldian fungi, a group of mitosporic fungi that live in freshwater with branched or sigmoidial spores, often growing on dead leaves in streams; smuts of aquatic plants; and certain yeasts.
EN: The cell, hypha, or coil of Ascomycetes that later becomes the ascoma, or part of it.
EN: A small spot-like apothecium, as in the lichen Arthonia. From Latin ardere, to sprinkle.
[医] 晕; 细隙, 小区
EN: A delimited space on a surface, separated from others by fissures or cracks.

EN: A method of thallic conidiogenesis that converts a hyphal element into a conindium (also called an arthrospore), fragmenting the hypha. Common in many basidiomycetes. Compare with holothallic. From Gr. arthron, joint.
abbr. 〈美(=Air Service Command)空军后勤司令部
[网络] 升序(ascending);非典型鳞状细胞(Atypical squamous cells);乙肝病毒携带者
EN: A prefix meaning sac, bladder, or ascus. From Gr. askós, vessel, bag, or wineskin.
EN: The asci-bearing fruiting body of Ascomycetes.

EN: A phylum of fungi characterized by the presence of an ascus, a sac-like structure where ascospores are produced. The largest group of fungi. Includes cup fungi or Discomycetes; most dermatophytes; the mycobiont part of most lichens; powdery mildews; and fungi that produce truffles.

EN: Spores formed in the developing ascus, generally as a result of karyogamy (nuclear fusion) followed by meiosis. Commonly, four haploid daughter nuclei divide to make eight haploid nuclei, around which eight ascospores are created by depositing wall material around them, a process sometimes called free cell formation.

EN: The reproductive cell of ascomycetes; where ascospores form and are contained. While sometimes traditionally restricted to only sexual reproduction, purely asexual mitosporic fungi have since been classified as having asci as well (List of mitosporic Ascomycota).
a. 吸收的, 同化的
EN: Hyphae related to growth, nutrition, and asexual reproduction as opposed to sexual reproduction; the soma.
a. 土著的, 土生土长的, 本地的
EN: 1. Indigenous, especially to a type of soil or earth.
单性接合孢子, [植]无配合子

EN: A spore close in form to a zygospore, but developed asexually (parthogenesis). Found in many species of Mucorales and some species of Entomophthorales, such as Entomophthora muscae. The structure that contains it is called an azygosporangium.
EN: A forcibly discharged basidiospore; the most typical kind. Compare with statismospore. From Latin ballista.
EN: A basidium-producing organ; the fruiting body of Basidiomycota.

EN: A phylum of fungi. Generally defined by sexual reproduction via basidiospores formed from a basidium, although a few purely anamorphic basidiomycetes exist. Typically mycelial, although some are yeasts and some are dimorphic. Basidiomycetes include earth balls; earthstars; false truffles; jelly fungi; many mushrooms; polypores; puffballs; most rusts; most smuts; and stinkhorns.
EN: A propagative sexual spore produced on a basidium, typically following karyogamy and meiosis, typically containing one or two haploid nuclei.
n. 孢子台, 芽孢台
EN: A cell or organ where basidiospores are produced, generally four. Basidia are characteristic of basidiomycetes. From Greek basis, base.
EN: A chain of conidia in which new spores are formed at the base and the oldest are at the apex. Compare with acropetal.

EN: One of the two basic forms of conidiogenesis, with thallic conidiogenesis. Characterized by the enlargement of the conidia initial before it is delimited by a septum. In holoblastic, both inner and outer walls of the blastic conidiogenous cell contribute to the formation of the conidium; in enteroblastic, only the inner walls enlarge and contribute. Monoblastic is from a single conidiogenous locus; polyblastic is when a conindiogenous cell has multiple conidiogenous loci.

EN: An asexual spore that forms by budding. One of the conidia types that can be produced in blastic conidiogenesis. Examples include yeasts such as Candida glabrata and Kloeckera, and the plant pathogenic Monilinia and Cladosporium mold.

EN: An iconic variety of mushroom characterized by fleshy fruit bodies and a poroid hymenophore (marked by pores rather than the gill-marked cap of agarics). They are often edible. Boletes are members of the order Boletales.
a. 萌芽的, 发育期的, 初露头角的

EN: A type of asexual cellular multiplication. A small outgrowth or bud from a parent cell enlarges and eventually separates from the parent cell. Typical in yeasts and many molds. Sometimes divided by how many buds are made, with monopolar, bipolar, and multipolar budding for one/two/many respectively.

EN: A compact multicellular propagule, with its thin-walled, undifferentiated cells produced in acropetal succession from the hyphae. Superficially resembles plant tissue at maturity (pseudoparenchymatous) such as raspberries, hence the resemblance to bulbils in botany. Found in certain basidiomycetes; characteristic of aero-aquatic fungi such as Bulbillomyces farinosus, where they grow on leaves or tree branches previously submerged in water.
n. [植]头状花序, 聚生花,小头,骨端
EN: The stalked, globose, apical apothecium of lichens of the order Caliciales.
n. 胶囊, 蒴果, 瓶帽, 航天舱
EN: A clear, gelatinous covering or sheath around the cell wall of certain yeasts, e.g. Cryptococcus, and some ascospores such as those of Sordaria fimicola.
vi. 吹毛求疵, 挑剔
EN: Combining forms meaning "fruit". From Gr. karpós, fruit.
vt. 连接, 把...连接成链状
EN: Arranged in chains or end-to-end series. Catenulate is the diminutive form for small chains. From Latin catena, a chain.
n. 几丁质, 壳多糖
[化] 壳多糖; 几丁质; 甲壳质
EN: A nitrogen-containing polysaccharide found in many fungal cell walls, generally as part of a chitin-glucan complex. From Gr. chiton, tunic.
EN: An obsolete division of fungi, meaning possessing mycelium; subsumed by Eumycota in later literature.
[网络] 几丁质酶体;壳糖复合体;几丁质合成酶存在于壳质体
EN: A small spheroidal organelle in many fungi that synthesizes chitin using chitin synthase zymogen, to use for cell wall synthesis.
EN: An asexual thick-walled spore developed from hyphae, generally for perennation rather than dissemination. From Gr. chlamys, cloak, -ydos, spore.
[网络] 壶菌门;瓶菌门;亚菌门

EN: A phylum of fungi. Informally known as chytrids. Characterized by chitinous cell walls and reproduction via zoospores, which are usually uniflagellate in the posterior although rarely polyflagellate. Many are saprobes that live in freshwater (see aquatic fungi) or the soil.
n. 卷须, 蔓足, 触毛
EN: A curl-like tuft; usually refers to a tendril-like mass of forced-out spores.
EN: A hyphal outgrowth that makes a connection during cell division between the resulting two cells by fusion. Generally associated with mycelium of Basidiomycetes.
a. 棍棒状的, 一端膨大的
EN: Narrowing at the base and then thickening; club-shaped.
EN: A closed fruit body that has no pre-defined opening; opens by rupture. Seen, e.g., in ascoma of Thielavia or in Erysiphales.
[网络] 腔胞纲;腔孢菌;腔孢菌纲
EN: An artificial taxon for mitosporic fungi with pycnidial and acervular states, i.e. they form their spores in an internal cavity. From Gtk. koilos, hollow.
EN: Prefix meaning "multinucleate". From Gr. koinós, shared or in common.
a. [生]多核细胞的, 多核体的
EN: Hyphae that lack septa and are multi-nucleate; seen in Zygomycota and Oomycota. From Gr. kytos, cell. Distinct from a synctium, a multinucleate structure resulting from fusion of protoplasts.
n. 殖民地, 移民队
[医] 菌(集)落, 菌丛; 移民区
EN: A massed group of hyphae and spores of a single species, especially if all are grown from a single spore (e.g. in a lab).
n. 小柱, 螺的轴柱, 蒴轴
EN: A sterile central axis within a fruiting body (sporocarp) or sporangium.
vt. 弄复杂, 使错综, 使恶化
EN: Bent or folded on itself. From Latin plicare, to fold.
EN: The process of producing conidia. Subdivided into blastic and thallic conidiogenesis.
EN: Producing conidia. Generally used as "conidiogenous cell", fertile cells that produce conidia; or "conidiogenous locus", for the particular point on a hypha or a cell where conidia are generated.
[网络] 载孢体;分生孢子器官
EN: Any multi-hyphal, conidia-bearing structure. An umbrella term that includes various traditional conidia-bearing structures such as a synnema, a sporodochium, an acervulus, or a pycnidium.
EN: A specialized hypha bearing or consisting of conidiogenous cells upon which conidia develop.
EN: A thin-walled, asexual spore borne on specialized hypha known as conidiophores. From Gr. konidion, diminutive of konis (dust).
a. 生长在粪便上的, 嗜粪癖的
EN: Growing or living on animal dung.
EN: A thick outer-covering or rind, generally of a fruiting body. From Latin cortice, bark.
EN: Of agarics, the remnants of the partial veil, frequently web-like, that covers mature gills. Thin and evanescent; eventually breaks up and disappears.
EN: The hook of an ascogenous hypha before development of the ascus.
a. 十字形的, 十字状的
EN: In the form of a cross.
a. 长成外壳状的, 紧贴在土壤(岩石)的

EN: Crust-like or having a hard surface layer, e.g. in a sporocarp; in lichens, a thallus firmly fixed to the substratum by the whole of their lower surface, generally lacking a distinct lower cortex.
EN: A break in the lower cortex of a lichen thallus which appears as a cup-like structure or marking. Characteristic of Sticta. From Gr. kyphella, the hollow of an ear.
EN: A large, sterile cell on the surface of a basidioma, particularly the hymenium from which it frequently projects.
a. 有齿的, 锯齿状的, 齿状的
n. 小齿, 齿状装饰
EN: A small, tooth-like projection, especially one on which spores are borne.
n. 皮肤真菌, 表皮寄生菌
EN: A parasitic fungus that focuses on tissue with keratin (skin, hair, nails) of humans and animals. Associated with the genera Epidermophyton, Microsporum, and Trichophyton.
EN: The skin condition caused by a dermatophyte infection.
a. 二分的, 叉状分枝的
[医] 二分的; 二叉的, 二歧的
EN: Forking into roughly equal pairs, often repeatedly, e.g. in hyphal branching. Compare with monopodial.
EN: Divided by intersecting septa in more than one plane, both transverse and longitudinal; a muriform spore. Found in Alternaria alternata as an example.
EN: A two-celled spore divided by a single septum. Usually applied to mitosporic fungi. Compare with amerospore and phragmospore.
EN: A subkingdom of Fungi that includes Ascomycota and Basidiomycota, or "higher fungi."
EN: A single cell (dikaryon) having two genetically distinct haploid nuclei.
a. 双晶的, 同时具有两种特性的, 二形的, 二态的
EN: Having two forms, e.g. both yeast and mycelial forms. Examples include Histoplasma and Sporothrix.
EN: A life cycle with two types of zoospores (dimorphic), primary and secondary.

EN: A class of saucer-shaped and cup-shaped Ascomycetes in which the hymenium is exposed at maturity; one in which the fruit body is an apothecium (discocarp). Prominent members include Pezizales, Helotiales, Ostropales, and Lecanorales.

EN: An evanescent connective, consisting of either a cell or cell wall material. It develops through the pores of septal lamellae of adjoining conidia in a chain, before later fragmenting and releasing the conidia.
EN: A septum found in Basidiomycetes that flares out in the middle to form a channel.
a. 有刺的, 有棘皮的
EN: Having sharply pointed spines, e.g. of spores. Its diminutive is echinulate, for delicate spines. Sometimes synonymous with spinose. From Gr. echinos, hedgehog.
a. 贫瘠的, 枯竭的, 衰微的
EN: Past the bearing period; overmature, e.g. a fruiting body that has emptied its spores.
v. 涌出, 流出, 泻出
EN: Expanded; stretched out flat, e.g. a film-like growth. From Latin fundere, to pour.
abbr. 日本株式会社远藤公司
EN: Prefix meaning "inner" or "inside", from Gr. éndon.
a. [生]生物内生的,体内(寄)生的,组织内寄生的
EN: Growing within anther living organism.
[医] 内寄生菌, 植物内寄生菌

EN: An organism that lives within a plant; in mycology, specifically fungi that live within plants but do not show external signs or damage to the plants. This is usually endomycorrhizial fungi in root systems and asymptomatic fungi in aerial plant parts
EN: 1. An endogenous spore, e.g. a sporgangiospore, often resembling an ascospore.
[医] 毛内癣菌, 毛内的
EN: Living within hair. Generally associated with parasitic dermatophyte infections.
[生]外生的, 体外生的, 残遗物, [生]残遗种
EN: Growing on the outer surface of another organism.
EN: A thin layer on top of the cortex; e.g. a sugar-like layer over some Parmeliaceae lichens or a layer on the apothecium of some Pezizales
a. 直立的, 竖立的, 笔直的
vt. 使竖立, 使直立, 树立, 建立
EN: 1. A disease of cereals and grasses caused by the fungus Claviceps.
a. 突然现出的, 迸出的, 裂出的
EN: Breaking through the surface of the substratum.
n. 民族真菌学( 研究各社会中对致幻蘑菇及其他真菌的使用)
EN: The study of the use of fungi by human cultures.

EN: Thalli where reproductive structures only develop on limited portions during fructication. The rest of the thallus remains in its original assimilative function. Compare holocarpic. If they have one sporangium, they are monocentric; if they have several sporgangia, they are polycentric. The vast majority of fungi are eucarpic.

EN: Fungi. From Greek for "true fungi". Generally used to distinguish fungi from related Pseudofungi traditionally also studied in mycology, as well as recently separated sister organisms such as Rozellida. The four traditional phyla of (true) fungi are Ascomycota, Basidiomycota, Chytridiomycota, and Zygomycota; Glomeromycota and Microsporidia have split off more recently.
a. 逐渐消失的, 容易消散的, 短暂的
[医] 易消灭的, 渐消失的, 挥发性的
EN: Having a short existence; soon disappearing, e.g. of a veil, an annulus, etc. From Latin evanscere, to disappear.
EN: Invasive, not indigenous; especially for organisms not adapted to a particular soil.
n. 仙人圈(一种小食品); 仙环
EN: Mushrooms or puffballs forming in a circle, started from a central mycelium in the soil. Fairy rings expand with time if undisturbed, and are generally associated with basidiomycetes.
a. 镰状的, 钩状的
EN: Curved, like a sickle or scythe. From Latin falx and falcis, sickle.

EN: A chemical change caused by enzymes of living organisms. In mycology, typically yeasts and molds performing anaerobic breakdowns such as changing carbohydrates to carbon dioxide and alcohol. Part of the creation of fermented foods and fermented drinks (most notably alcoholic beverages).
n. 细丝, 细线, 灯丝, 单纤维
[化] 长丝; 单丝(复丝中的单根细丝); 丝极
EN: A fine thread. Commonly used for hyphal threads or other simple thread-like fungal structures. From Latin filum, thread.
a. 细丝状的, 如丝的, 纤维所成的
EN: 1. Thread-like, or composed of filaments.
a. 丝状的, 纤维状的, 线状的
[医] 线形的; 线形探条
EN: In the shape of a thread; thin.
EN: Soft, not cartilaginous or wood-like. Associated with agarics and boletes.
a. 弯曲的, 动摇不定的, 不稳定的, 波状的
EN: Wavy. From Latin flexus, bend.
a. 羊毛状的, 絮状的
EN: Fluffy or cottony; byssoid. Common among many colonies of fungi. Its diminutive form is flocculose, for a small and delicate floccose element. From Latin floccus, a tuft of wool.
EN: The aethalium of Fuligo septica. Commonly found in tannin-containing tubs drying hides into leather.
n. 流溢, 面红, 旺盛, 发烧, 惊飞的鸟, 同花牌
a. 丰足的, 齐平的, 满盈的, 泛滥的
adv. 齐平地, 直接地
vi. 脸发红, 奔涌, 旺盛, 惊飞
vt. 淹没, 冲洗, 使脸红, 使激动, 使齐平, 使惊飞
EN: The rapidly growing stage of a mycelium, especially in mushrooms.
a. 叶上生的, 寄生在叶上的(如某些真菌,水藻等)
EN: Living on leaves, e.g. foliicolous lichen.
a. 多叶的, 叶子覆盖的
EN: 1. A hyphal cell that supports a sporogenous cell or thallus, specifically the support of the conidiophore in Aspergillus and the macroconidium of Fusarium.
EN: A phosphorescent light emitted by moist, decaying wood; one of the most famous forms of fungal bioluminescence.
a. 自由的, 享受政治权力的, 允许的, 免费的, 丰富的
vt. 释放, 解放, 使自由
EN: Not adhering; not attached to the stipe, esp. of lamellae or tubes. Compare with adnate.
EN: Living on fruit. From Latin fructus, fruit.
EN: Living on shrubs. From Latin frutex, shrubs.

EN: A substance able to kill fungi, especially at low concentration. From Latin caedere, to kill. Generally used for chemical substances rather than heat, light, radiation, etc. which are called sterilization instead.
[医] 真菌样的, 蕈状的
EN: Similar to a fungus in texture or morphology.
n. 真菌, 真菌类植物
[医] 真菌, 霉菌, , 蕈, 海绵肿

EN: A kingdom of organisms in Eukaryota. Fungi are distinguished based on their morphology, nutritional modes, and ecology. Typical traits are that they lack plastids, are osmotrophic (absorb nutrients from their environment), are never phagotrophic, lack an ameboid pseudopodal phase, cell walls are composed of a chitin-glucan complex, mitochondria have flattened cristae and perioxomes are nearly always present, and are mostly non-flagellate; flagella when present lack mastigonemes. From Gr. sphongos, σπόγγος, sponge.
EN: Cord-like. From Latin funis, rope.
EN: (Of hyphae) Aggregated into cord-like strands.
EN: Covered with bran-like particles; scurfy.
a. 纺锭状的, 两端渐细的
EN: Spindle-shaped; narrowing toward the ends. Of spores, stipe, cystidia, etc. From Latin fusus, spindle.
a. 盔状的, 戴盔的
EN: Hooded; hat-shaped. From Latin galea, helmet.
EN: A sexual cell; a uninucleate haploid reproductive cell capable of fusing with another. From Gr. gámos, marriage, union.
n. 芽, 无性芽, 芽体
[医] 芽, 微胶粒, 分子团
EN: 1. Another term for chlamydospores, sometimes restricted to specifically spores that broke free from the mycelium to be dispersed, often via water. From Latin gemma, "jewel"
a. 有膝状关节的, 弯曲成膝状的
a. 在地上或土中生长的, 在地下结果的
EN: Preferring an environment in soil, as in Microsporum cookei or fungi that produce truffles.
EN: A hole in a spore wall, frequently apical, through which it germinates. Germ tubes emerge through it. Associated with rusts.
EN: A sporangium at the end of a germ tube. Originates by germination of an oospore or of a zygosporangium.

EN: A short hypha that sprouts from the germ pore during germination. If conditions are favorable, will form a full mycelium. In plant pathogenic fungi, forms an appressorium, from which the infective hypha spread and penetrate the tissues of the host.
a. 无毛的, 光滑的, 光洁的
EN: Smooth, not hairy; e.g. of the surface of a pileus or stipe.
EN: The central, internal portion of the fruiting body of Gasteromycetes and underground Pezizales.
a. 球状的, 球形的
a. 滴状的, 有斑点的
EN: 1. Having tear-like drops. From Latin gutta, drop.
EN: Spores bearing one or more guttules (oil-like drops) inside, e.g. the ascospores of Podospora comata.
EN: A small drop or drop-like particle, especially oil-like globules in a spore resembling a nucleus.
[网络] 粘菌门;裸菌门;裸真菌门
EN: An obsolete division of fungi, characterized as having a plasmodium. Subsumed by Myxomycota (true slime molds) in later literature.
EN: An ascoma in which the perithecium is in a loose hyphal network.
vi. 旋转, 不停地转动
EN: Curved; folded and wavy, like a brain.
钩骨, 具钩的, 钩状的
EN: Collective term for hyphae and tissues between asci; interascal tissue.
EN: A hyphal branch for absorption of food. It penetrates the wall of the living host cell. Found in certain parasitic fungal plant pathogens, such as Phytophthora.
EN: Having two or more genetically distinct nuclei in a common cytoplasm, making a combined cell.
异鞭毛的, 不等鞭毛的
EN: 1. A grouping of organisms within Chromista that includes Pseudofungi.

EN: In lichens, when the thallus is stratified. The photobiont is distributed in a compact layer, and the hyphal tissue of the fungi are separated into an outer rind and an inner stratum. From Gr. hetero, different, and meros, part.
EN: Fungi that require the interaction of two different thalli for sexual conjugation to occur.
n. 核, 粒心, 脐
[医] 门, 种脐(种子), 皮片蒂(整形手术)
EN: A scar after a spore is discharged; was previously the point of attachment of a basidiospore to the sterigma. From Latin hilum, mask.
a. 灰白的, 陈旧的
EN: Covered thickly with silk-like hairs, especially of a pileus or stipe, often grayish or white.

EN: Having all of the thallus converted into the fruiting body at the end of maturation; compare eucarpic. The somatic and reproductive phases do not coexist as a result. Examples include Olpidiaceae and Synchytriaceae.
EN: Term describing the whole fungus throughout all its morphs (states, phases). Generally includes a single teleomorph phase and one or more anamorph phases.
EN: A method of thallic conidiogenous in which a hyphal element is converted as a whole into a single conidium. All the cell wall layers are involved. Compare with arthric. From Gr. holos, whole.
EN: In lichens, when the photobiont is are distributed uniformly or at random throughout the thallus. From Gr. homoios, similar.
EN: Having genetically identical (or near-identical) nuclei, e.g. in a mycelium.
同宗配合(现象), 同宗接合(现象)
EN: The condition where sexual reproduction can occur in a single thallus, without the interaction of two separate thalli.
EN: Preferring an aquatic habitat. Common among zygomycetes, as zoospores rely on water to move.
a. 生活在水中或湿地的,喜湿的
EN: Preferring a moist habitat. Common among fungi.
a. 湿度计的, 吸湿性的, 易潮湿的
EN: 1. Becoming soft in wet air, hard in dry; readily absorbing moisture from the atmosphere.
EN: The spore-bearing fruiting surface of Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes. An aggregation of asci or basidia in a layer (palisade) mixed with other sterile cells.
子实层柄, 子实层体
EN: The portion of a basidioma or ascoma bearing the hymenium.
EN: A single filament of a mycelium. From Gr. hyphe, weaving.
EN: Of, or pertaining to, a hypha.
[医] 丝状菌类, 不[完]全菌纲
EN: An artificial class of mitosporic fungi that reproduces asexually. Traditionally subdivided into Agonomycetales, Hyphomycetales, Stilbellales, and Tuberculariales.
EN: A thick-walled resting spore; germinates only after a lapse of weeks or months. From Gr. hypnos, sleep.
[化] 硫代硫酸钠; 五水合硫代硫酸钠; (俗称)海波
[医] 疑病, 海波, 硫代硫酸钠, 皮下注射, 皮下注射
EN: Prefix meaning "under" or "lower". From Gr. hypo.

EN: 1. (Of lichens) The first growth of the hyphae, before differentiation has taken place. Usually of a crustaceous lichen's earliest stage, lacking a cortex and photobiont. Often persists as a colored layer on the bottom of the later stages of maturation.

EN: Not operculate; lacking an operculum. Generally refers to asci or sporangia that discharge spores by an irregular apical opening or pore instead. Found in various Discomycetes and most other ascomycetes.
a. 闰的, 插入中间的, 被夹于中间的
EN: 1. (of growth) Between the apex and the base; not apical. From Latin intercalare, to insert.

EN: A propagule for lichen growth; can both increase the surface area of a lichen and become detached from the thallus to disperse the lichen. Isidia are structures larger than soredia, and contain both the mycobiont and the photobiont. They are usually cylindrical, but can also be verrucose, clavate, and other shapes.
EN: Zoospores with flagella of roughly equal length. Seen in Ectrogella bacillariacearum and other aquatic zoosporic fungi. From Gr. kontos, a pole.
EN: Fungi of the Tremellales or trembling fungi. Known for having a soft, elastic consistency, similar to gelatin or jelly.
n. 吴雨霏(香港女歌手)
EN: A prefix meaning "nucleus." From Gr. karyon.
n. [生物] 同性配子之互相融合
EN: The final stage in the fusion of two sexual nuclei, after plasmogamy, that forms the zygote nucleus, but before meiosis.
EN: An organelle that is the base of a zoospore flagellum. Connected to the nuclear membrane by means of a rhizoplast. Found in Blastocladia and Rhizophydiales, for example.
EN: Flask-shaped; swollen at base, narrowed at top.
n. 薄板, 薄层, 薄片

EN: A gill; a hymenium-covered vertical plate, generally of an agaric. Attaches to the stipe in a variety of ways, including: free, unattached; adnate, attached; adnexed, a partial attachment; sinuate, similar to adnate but with an S-shaped curve; decurrent, attached and also running further down the surface of the stipe. From Latin lamina, a thin plate.
a. 有薄层的, 薄片形的
EN: Like wool; covered with short-hair-like elements.
n. 侧部, 支线, 边音
a. 侧面的, 旁边的
EN: At the side, e.g. of a stipe.
EN: A milk-like juice that flows from some fungi when cut or damaged, as in Lactarius.
a. 制成格状的, 装有格子的
EN: Cross-barred. (See also Clathrus, lattice-work fungus, especially Clathrus ruber.)
a. 透镜的, 扁豆似的
[医] 豆状核的, 晶状体的, 透镜状的, 透镜的
EN: Shaped like a double convex lens.
EN: Covered in small scales; for example, the pileus of Lepiota.
n. 青苔, 地衣, 苔藓病

EN: A dual organism that arises from an association of fungi (mycobiont) and algae or cyanobacteria (photobiont). The two coexist in a mutualistic relationship as partners; the resulting lifeform differs markedly from its isolated components.
EN: Growing on or in lichens. Can apply to both lichenicolous fungus and other lichens.
n. [植] 苔粉, 地衣多糖苔藓
EN: A polycarbohydrate found in wall of the hyphae of many lichen-forming fungi, most characteristically Iceland moss.
EN: The scientific study of lichens.
n. [地]地衣测量年代法( 指用测量地衣直径来确定其生长年代或其生长地区年代的方法)

EN: A technique for studying the exposure age of rock surfaces based on the size and diameter of lichen thalli. Used extensively in glaciology. Most frequently uses map lichen for dating. Lichenometry has been used to date Easter Island moai among other elements.
a. 似木的, 木质的, 木制的
EN: Wood-like; having the consistency of wood, such as the fruiting body in Fomes, Ganoderma, or other Aphyllophorales.
EN: Living in or on wood, although not necessarily deriving nourishment from it, as do wood-decay fungi.
[医] 腔, 流明(光通单位)
EN: The central cavity of a structure, usually referring to a cell bounded by tissue or cell walls.
EN: Fungi that exhibit bioluminescence, emitting light in certain conditions.
a. 新月状的, 半月形的
EN: Crescent-shaped, like a crescent moon. Sometimes synonymous with falcate. From Latin luna, moon.
EN: In fungi with multiple types of conidia, the larger; compare microconidia, mesoconidia.
EN: Large fungi with visible sporocarps, such as mushrooms.
EN: Having a morphologically different conidiophore from the vegetative hyphae; a specialized conidiophore.
a. 有斑点的, 有污点的
vt. 使有斑点, 使有污点
n. 斗篷, 罩子, 披风
EN: A layer of hyphae covering the roots of ectomycorrhizal plants, generally trees. Connected to a Hartig net on the inside, and extramatrical hyphae on the outside.
EN: In agarics and boletes, a proliferation of hyphae on the edge of the pileus that protects the developing hymenium.
n. 母体, 子宫, 基质, 脉石, 模型, 矩阵
EN: 1. The substance in or on which a fungus grows.
EN: The use of fungi such as yeast in medicines.
n. 成熟分裂, 减数分裂
[医] 减数分裂, 成熟分裂

EN: A series of two successive nuclear divisions that reduces the number of chromosomes by one-half, going from a diploid state to a haploid one. The last part of the sexual phase in many fungi, following plasmogamy and karyogamy. Contrast with mitosis.

EN: A sporangium that is a cylindrical outgrowth from the swollen tip of a sporangiophore. A chain-like row of sporangiospores are produced there. Characteristic of Mucorales; also found in some other zygomycetes.
EN: All of the microorganisms present in an area, including algae, bacteria, protozoa, and fungi. Compare mycobiota.
小分生孢子; 小型分生孢子
EN: In fungi with multiple types of conidia, the smaller; compare macroconidia, mesoconidia.
EN: 1. Having hyphae of small diameter.
EN: 1. Fungi that grow on host plants. Subdivided into powdery mildew ("true"), downy mildew ("false"), and dark mildew.
[医] 有丝分裂, [间接]核分裂
EN: The normal division of a nucleus. Results in two child nuclei with the same number of chromosomes as the parent.
EN: A thin-walled sporangium of certain Blastocladiales producing uninucleate diploid zoospores (mitospores) by mitosis.
EN: A zoospore from a mitosporangium. From Gr. mitos, thread.
EN: Purely asexual fungi that reproduce by mitosis.
n. 模子, 模型, 霉
v. 形成, 塑造, 发霉
EN: A fungus of very small size, usually with microscopic sporocarps.
EN: Cells having a single nucleus each; having genetically identical haploid nuclei (monokaryon or haplont). Found, for example, in the mycelium of Agaricales.

EN: A type of branching where there is a persistent main axis from which branches split from, one at a time, often in alternate or spiral series. Often uses acropetal succession. Compare with dichotomous.
EN: Form. From Gr. μορφή, morphḗ, form.

EN: Flowerless plants; not fungi. However, some lichens were given misnomers in the past that misidentified them as mosses, including oakmoss, Swedish moss, dyer's moss, Iceland moss, beard moss, and reindeer moss.
a. 能动的, 运动表象型的
a. 粘液质的, 粘的, 分泌粘液的
[医] 胶浆性的, 胶粘的, 粘性的
EN: Sticky or viscous when wet; slimy. Present in many fungi and especially slime molds.
[生化]I adj.黏液样的(亦作 mucoidal)
EN: Like mucus, having the consistency of mucilage; slimy.
EN: A division of fungi broken off from Zygomycota in the 2010s that includes many of the molds, microscopic fungi. Includes Mucorales, the largest and most closely studied order of zygomycetes.
EN: Having more than one septum.
EN: Spores arranged like bricks in a wall; having both longitudinal and transverse septa. From Latin murus, wall.
n. 蘑菇形物, 蘑菇, 暴发户
vi. 迅速生长, 迅速增加, 采蘑菇
a. 蘑菇形的, 迅速生长的
EN: Large agarics, or other fleshy fungi such as boletes. Commonly divided into mushrooms (human-edible) and toadstools (inedible).
EN: Combining prefixes that mean "fungus". From Gr. mykēs and mykētos (μύκης), fungus.
EN: A discrete aggregation of hyphae. Compared to a rhizomorph, it is undifferentiated from other hyphae and has no apical meristem.
EN: A mass of hyphae or fungal filaments; the thallus.
EN: Fungi. As a suffix (-mycetes), the recommended ending for the names of fungal classes.
EN: Poisoning by larger fungi, usually mushrooms.
EN: A fungal disease of the skin, usually of the foot.
EN: The fungal part of a lichen.
EN: Aggregate fungal life in the area under consideration; equivalent of the term flora in plants or fauna in animals.
EN: Coming from fungi; growing on fungi.
EN: The scientific study of fungi. From Gr. lógos, discourse.

EN: A symbiotic association between a fungus and the root system of a plant, usually trees. Traditionally subdivided into ectotrophic, where the fungus forms a sheaf on the surface of the root to create a 'Hartig net', and endotropic, where fungal hyphae directly enter the cortical cells of the root. Later, more precise divisions included ectomycorrhiza, arbuscular mycorrhiza, ericoid mycorrhiza, orchid mycorrhiza, arbutoid mycorrhiza, and monotropoid mycorrhiza.
EN: Fungal diseases of humans and animals (rarely, plants as well).
EN: The recommended ending of the name of fungal phyla.
EN: Toxins (the product of one organism injurious to another) produced by fungi. Studied by mycotoxicology. Poisonings are called mycotoxicoses.
[网络] 粘菌门;黏菌门;粘细菌

EN: True slime molds. No longer categorized as fungi, but were formerly categorized as such in older literature, and still studied in mycology; now considered part of Amorphea. Since reclassified as Myxogastria. From Gr. myxa, slime.
EN: Predatory fungi that trap, devour, and digest nematodes in the soil.
贵腐病, 贵腐酒;贵霉菌
EN: A condition from the mold Botrytis growing on overripe grapes. Used in the production of certain sweet wines.
EN: (of spores, stipe, cystidia, etc.) The reverse of clavate; widest at the base.
EN: The reverse of egg-shaped or ovoid; the narrower end is on bottom.
EN: The reverse of pear-shaped or pyriform.
n. [生]卵原细胞, 藏卵器
EN: The female sexual organ of Oomycetes, which at maturity contains one or more oospores. From Gr. gonos, progeny.

EN: Water molds. Traditionally considered fungi, but now classed as closer to algae. Part of the Chromista kingdom. Contain cellulose in their cell walls rather than chitin, and coenocytic hypae rather than septate hyphae.
EN: Female gamete of oomycetes; "egg" of the oogonium.
EN: The resting spore formed as a result of fertilization of the oosphere. Has a thick, resistant wall. Subdivided into centric, subcentric, subeccentric, and eccentric oospores by its structure.
[医] 盖, 岛盖, 盖(昆虫), 厣(软体动物), 鳃盖(鱼)
EN: A lid or cover. Usually refers to the lid-like apex of a sporangium or ascus found in some chytrids and Pezizales.
n. 苔色素, 染料衣(产生苔色素之地衣)
EN: A reddish-purple dye traditionally extracted from lichen.
EN: Absorbing nutrients from surroundings via osmosis. True of all fungi.
EN: 1. A cavity ending in a pore at the neck of a perithecium (ascocarp) of ascomycetes.
a. 卵形的, 梨形的
EN: Egg-shaped; the narrower end is on top.
n. 乳头, 小乳头状突起, 丘疹, 小脓疱
EN: A small rounded elevation. Generally refers to an elevation on the wall of the sporangium which on breaking serves as the exit point of zoospores and planogametes.

EN: A sterile upward-growing, basally-attached hypha in a hymenium, especially in ascomata of ascomycetes where they are generally filiform and clavate. The free ends frequently converge toward the ostiole and make a structure called an epithecium over the asci. Part of the hamathecium. Has a number of minor variants distinguished by names such as paraphysoid, pseudoparaphysis, pseudophysis, dikaryoparaphysis, and hyphidium.
EN: A layer of tissue that joins the stipe to the edge of the pileus in agarics, covering the gills during hymenium development. May become an annulus or a cortina after development is complete.
a. 梳状的, 齿形的
EN: Resembling the teeth of a comb, e.g. of the margin of a pileus.
EN: A small or slender stalk.
n. 薄皮, 薄膜, 分光薄膜
EN: An asexual conidial head in the shape of a brush. Consists of a pedicel or conidiophore that supports a cluster of conidiogenous cells (phialides). Characteristic of Penicillium stipes.
EN: 1. Conidiogenous cell growth where a conidiophore or germ tube grows through a preexisting pore.
n. [植]( 某些真菌的) 包被
EN: The outer wall of a sporangium or other fruiting body. Can be either acellular or composed of plectenchyma.
n. [植]( 某些真菌的)子囊壳
EN: A rounded, oval ascocarp, characteristic of Pyrenomycetes and pyrenolichens. Can commonly be pyriform, obpyriform, beaked, or lageniform.

EN: Feeding by engulfing food; extending a pseudopod or other protoplasmic extension, as seen in protozoa. Never seen in true fungi (Eumycota), but some Pseudofungi use this in addition to osmocytosis, e.g. Myxomycetes.

EN: A type of conidiogenous cell, bottle-shaped, that produces blastic conidia (phialospores) in basipetal succession. The philade itself does not increase in length. The most common conidiogenous cell among conidial fungi. From Gr. phiale, jar.
EN: An asexual spore formed from the tip of a phialide. Formed by abstriction.
EN: The photosynthetic element in a lichen. Either algae (a phycobiont) or cyanobacteria (a cyanobiont).
n. 趋光性, 向光性, 光致变色(现象)
EN: A tropic phenomenon driven by light, where growth curves toward or against light stimuli. For example, sporangiphores of Pilobus and Phycomyces direct themselves toward light.
EN: An asexual reproductive spore partitioned by two or more transverse septa. Most commonly found in mitosporic fungi. Compare with amerospore and didymospore.

EN: A group of forms alike in morphology. Often means a group of organisms that are potentially interbreeding. In plant pathology, it means a group with similar preferences in plants targeted; a race may be adapted to target only a single cultivar of a plant. Tracking the history of an organism is phylogeny. From Old Italian razza, generation.
[医] [热带]毛孢子菌病, 发结节病
EN: A fungal infection of the hair, characterized by stony, hard nodules along hair shafts. A type of dermatocytosis.
EN: The cap of basidiomata that bears the fertile hymenium.
a. 毛多的, 有毛的
EN: Covered with long, soft filaments; hairy. Oudemansiella pilosa is an example. From Latin pilus, hair.
n. 原质体, 合胞体, 变形体, 疟原虫

EN: A motile mass seen in the growth phase of acellular slime molds. Generally multinucleate and lacking cell walls. See also protoplasmodium, aphanoplasmodium, phaneroplasmodium, filoplasmodium, and pseudoplasmodium.

EN: The fusion of two cells or plasmodial cytoplasms, resulting in the nuclei juxtaposed and a dikaryon formed. In many sexual phases of fungi, the first step which precedes karyogamy (nuclear fusion) and meiosis.
EN: A thick, packed tissue of twisted hyphae formed during basidiocarp development as it enlarges and generative hyphae begin to differentiate. From Gr. plektos, to twist, and enchyma, infusion.
EN: 1. Fungi having more than one form in its life cycle, e.g. holomorphs comprising a teleomorph and one or more anamorphs.
EN: Growing from the sides, e.g. of hyphae.
n. 毛孔, 小孔, 气孔
vi. 专心阅读, 细想, 钻研, 沉思, 注视
EN: 1. A small opening, as in tretic conidiogenesis.
EN: A fungal disease caused by the water mold Phytophthora infestans; cause of the Great Famine of Ireland and other potato famines.
能发育成植物体的芽, 繁殖体

EN: Any structure that serves to spread the organism, both via propagation of new organisms as well as vegetatively increasing a single organism's size. In fungi, generally spores, bulbils, fragments of mycelium, isidia, soredia, and others.
EN: Prefix meaning "false", from Gr. pseudos.

EN: A subdivision of stramenopiles consisting of organisms similar to fungi and traditionally studied in mycology, including Oomycota, Hyphochytriomycota, Labyrinthulomycota, and Thraustochytriales. Contrasted with Eumycota, true fungi.
EN: Separated hyphal cells capable of germination.
EN: A type of plectenchyma made of tightly packed, angular or polyhedral cells.
EN: A stroma formed of both fungal tissue and remnant tissues of a host plant.
EN: Fruit body (basidioma) of Lycoperdales. Emits a cloud of spores when disturbed ("puffing").
EN: Very small (but still visible to unaided eyesight), e.g. with rust sori.
a. 正在腐烂的, 腐败的
EN: Decaying; becoming soft. From Latin putrescere, to grow rotten.
EN: An asexual fruiting body (conidioma), generally flask-shaped, lined entirely by conidiogenous cells.
n. 脊椎, 脊柱, 花序轴
[医] 脊柱, 脊椎, 花序轴, 叶轴
EN: A geniculate or zig-zag holoblastic extension of a conidiogenous cell from sympodial conidiogenous cell development. Such cells having a rachis are called rachiform. From Gr. ráchis, axis, spine.
EN: A hyphal cell having a swelling at one end, resembling a tennis racket; found in dermatophytes.
EN: Living on plant branches or twigs.
EN: Kidney-like or bean-like in form, e.g. of spores. From Latin renes, kidney, or faba, a broad bean.

EN: A slender, tapered structure of anucleate filaments bearing a superficial resemblance to a plant root, as it is extended by the thallus of chytrids as a feeding organ. Generally part of a root system-like aggregation of branched hyphae.

EN: A strand or cord of mycelium, often with a dark-colored rind surrounding a central core of colorless cells, penetrating a soft substratum or between portions of it (e.g. between bark and wood). Unlike a mycelial cord, features distinct tissue, unlike "normal" hyphae. Functions as organ of absorption of nutritive substances. Seen in some Agaricales and Gasteromycetes.
EN: A branched system of rhizoids that resembles a mycelium in chytrids.

EN: A sister group of quasi-fungi that lack chitinous cell walls. Traditionally considered chytrids, but have since been separated and reclassified in the 2010s. Phagotrophs rather than osmotrophes. Rozella, a group of obligate endoparasites, is possibly the earliest diverging lineage of fungi.
EN: 1. Living in wasteland, ruins, or debris.
EN: Wrinkled. Seen, e.g., in basidiospores of Panaeolina foenisecii. From Latin ruga, wrinkle or crease.
n. 锈, 生锈, 衰退
EN: 1. Plant diseases caused by fungi of the order Pucciniales.
EN: An organism that uses dead organic material as food.
n. 生于岩石间的, 生于岩石上的
a. 粗糙的, 多痂的, 难解决的, 猥亵的

EN: A hardened, often rounded, mass of hyphae, normally having no spores. May give rise to a fruit body, a stroma (as in ergot), conidiophores, or mycelium. Can be a store of nutrients as part of perennation; can reinitiate vegetative growth after conditions have improved and a season has passed.
a. 有盾状的, 有鳞甲的, 圆盾形的
[医] 鳞的, 鼓室盾板的
EN: Like a shield or round plate in shape. From Latin scutum, shield.

EN: A fruiting body with the appearance of an unopened agaric or bolete. The margin of the pileus does not break free of the columella-stipe, generally seen in vertical development (e.g. Podaxis pistillaris).
EN: Having a slightly morphologically different conidiophore from the vegetative hyphae.
EN: Living in seeds; seed-borne fungi. Examples include Ascochyta pisi, Colletotrichum lindemuthianum, Microdochium panattonianum, and others.
EN: 1. Growing old. From Latin senescere, to grow old.
a. 有中隔的, 有隔膜的
EN: Having septa; divided by partitions.
[化] 隔膜; 隔片; 隔墙; 隔板
EN: A cell wall in a hypha.
EN: Edged with teeth, like a comb or saw, e.g. of gills; its diminutive form is serrulate.
EN: The phase of the fungal life cycle when sexually reproductive cells and organs are formed. This term is preferred over sex in animals, as the fungal process is not equivalent.

EN: A eukaryotic lifeform that spreads via spores. Has both ameba (cellular slime molds) and plasmoidial (multi-nucleate) varieties. No longer categorized as fungi, but were formerly categorized as such in older literature. Cellular slime molds are part of Acrasiomycota or Dictyosteliomycota; plasmodial slime molds were traditionally part of the class Myxomycota, since renamed Myxogastria. From Gr. myxa, slime.
n. 煤尘, 污迹, 黑穗病

EN: 1. A class of destructive plant diseases, generally of cereal grasses, caused by parasitic fungi of Ustilaginomycetes. Distinguished by transformation of plant organs permeated by hyphae into a dark mass of spores.
n. 身体, 肉体, 身体细胞
EN: 1. The assimilative (sustaining) body of an organism, distinguished from reproductive parts or phases. From Gr. soma, body.
n. [生]拟无配子生殖, 体细胞配合

EN: The fusion of somatic (vegetative) cells during plasmogamy but not karyogamy. Found in the majority of basidiomycetes, many species of yeasts (such as Saccharomyces), and some chytrids (such as Chytriomyces).

EN: A propagule for vegetative lichen growth; a combination of phycobiont algae wrapped by mycobiont hyphae, and produced on a lichen thallus. Has the appearance of a powdery granule. From Latin soredium, a small heap.
EN: A heap of spores. Fruiting structure in certain fungi, including the spore mass of rusts, but also Acrasidae and Synchytriaceae. From Gr. soros, heap.
vt. 产卵, 酿成, 大量生产
vi. 产卵, 大量生产
EN: Mycelium used for starting fungal cultures, especially mushrooms; e.g. bricks of manure interlaced with mycelia.
[医] 棘状的; 棘的, 刺的; 棘突的
EN: A vesicle-rich body surrounded by actin filaments found in the growing tips of most fungi during periods of growth. Densely staining.
EN: Prefixes meaning "spore". From Gr. spora, seed.
EN: A small sporangium of Mucorales producing a small number of sporangiospores.
EN: A thallus element bearing one or more sporangia.
EN: A walled spore produced within a sporangium.
EN: A sac-like structure that produces spores endogenously. From Gr. angeion, vessel.
EN: A reproductive structure in fungi. Can result from both sexual and asexual processes.

EN: The layered wall defining a spore. Considered to have five layers. From within to outwards: the thin interior endosporium, the thick episporium, the exosporium (or tunic), the perisporium, and ectosporium, although the outermost two layers are fleeting and can be absorbed back into the perisporium and exosporium.
[植]芽胞房囊, 孢子果, 子实体
EN: A unit for production, protection, and dissemination of spores. Sometimes divided into ascocarp, basidiocarp, and zyogosporocarp.
EN: A cluster of conidiophores bearing the spore mass, like a cushion.
EN: A spore that is not forcibly discharged, unlike a ballistospore. Seen in the basidiospores of Gastromycetes. From Gr. statis, immobility.
a. 星形的, 似星的
EN: Like a star in form, especially spores.
[医] 担子柄; 叶座(种子植物)
EN: The small, spicule-like (pointed) pedicel or structure upon which a basidiospore forms. From Gr. sterigma, support.
